provenance.method: Fresh visual transcription of the 300 dpi scan: Arabic words, Bengali translation and every upper sign anchored to its letter.

unresolved.question: Surah header boxes print no Arabic surah name, so 'arabic' is null. Surah 109 Bengali name read as 'সূরা কা-ফিরূন' (ূ vs ু under র not fully certain).

Legend prints the band digits circled, but on the band they are printed without a circle, so enclosure is 'none'. The ৬ beside each ringed-wedge looks like a closed oval at scan resolution; recorded as plain ৬.
Row 1: the mark over the lam of فَوَيْلٌ is a blurred blob; read as dammatain (ٌ), which the next row's لِّلْمُصَلِّيْنَ (shadda on lam) supports.
Row 2 and row 7: ২ sits over nun sakin before ص/ت (ikhfa); label taken from the legend (দম ফেলিলে দুই আলিফ) but the fit is doubtful.

Row 7: the final alif of اَنَا has a small rounded zero (encoded U+06DF) and a solid down arrow in the band above it. The right-margin note beside rows 6-7 explains the arrow (alif not to be read/lengthened); its text is partly illegible, so the arrow's label_bn is a paraphrase. Arrow recorded with layer 'band' since it is printed in the band, not on the Arabic line.
Row 7: the waqf sign over verse circle 3 (after اَعْبُدُ) read as small ج (ۚ).

Row 0: the first word is printed اَرَءَيْتَ (hamza on its own seat with fatha); ya of يٰۤاَيُّهَا in row 6 is printed with a tall alif-like stroke and madda, encoded in the usual Indo-Pak form يٰۤاَيُّهَا.
The ruku sign ع beside verse circles 107:7 and 108:3, the QR codes and the margin ruku boxes are not encoded.
